scenarios.note: The conflated number: it overstates progress by roughly a third to a half. Shown only so the viewer can explain why it is wrong.

reading: Central range A-B: ~40-80 years at the recent pace. Five years would require ~300 mi/year of net closure (~7.7x the gross rate); 200 years would require ~7.5 mi/year net, well below any recent year. Closer to 20 years than to 200 only under a doubling.
caveats: Miles BUILT, miles CERTIFIED, and miles of road gap CLOSED are three different numbers. Only net gap closure moves the finish date; the build rate (~52/yr) overstates progress by roughly a third to a half.

Gross closure (39.0/yr) measures project output; net GIS closure (18.5/yr) measures progress toward completion and is the stricter figure — the gap is route-length growth and GIS re-measurement adding road miles even as old ones close.
Scenario H (29 years) is the number you get by conflating built miles with closed miles; it is shown only to avoid.
2017 miles built could not be verified (no NCTA annual/progress report or Form 990 figure located; ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer blocked in the research environment).
Scenario E is the most pessimistic defensible trend but rests on a 2015 on-road figure of a different vintage.
Finish years are end-2025 plus the years-to-finish, rounded.

epochs.note: Net is the robust figure (stable 1,829-1,924 mi across 100/200/400 m tolerances); gross new/gone are upper bounds mixing genuine construction with re-routes, re-digitization, and coverage change. 1982 baseline is thin (999.7 mi of 'existing' trail digitized); ND existing line in 1982 is only 1.4 mi; MN 113.9 mi.

Net stable 1,887-1,923 mi across 50/100/200 m. MINNESOTA TRAP: the 2005 dataset holds only 158.0 mi in MN (no Superior Hiking Trail), so most of MN's 780.7 'new' mi is coverage change, not construction. Clean additions: Vermont 70.6 mi (2019 extension, zero 'gone') and North Dakota 274.9 mi new. Of the 2,694.4 gross new mi, 1,599.1 are off-road and 1,095.3 on-road. The independent build-rate record (~52 mi/yr built 2015-2025) implies roughly 1,100 mi of genuine construction over 2005-2026, about 40% of the gross 'new' figure.

The 2016 NY/PA centerline (NPS IRMA Ref 2229138, Rowbotham 2016) carries only a metadata PDF with no retrievable geometry. No dated snapshot exists between May 2005 and November 2026, so the 2005->2026 epoch cannot be split at 2016 except via OSM, and only for Michigan.

OpenStreetMap relation 11140515. MAPPING dates, not build dates: a way appearing after 2020 may have been built earlier and only mapped later. The 2020 line is incomplete mapping (900.2 mi vs ~1,180 mi of route in MI). Net stable 262.6-262.7 mi across tolerances.
